rows: Technique is a melody until the hands find it. Show me the first note: the grip, then the turn.
Brawling sounds like a crowd singing badly, all voices at once. From the ring it becomes one line at a time.
A risk is a note held too long. Tell me which hold you will play when it begins to fade.
Slow is a long breath before the chorus. Then the next move arrives on time.
The people want a song they can hum on the way home. Give them a phrase they can carry.
I am here, and I know the tune I came to play.
I am known for a sound that carries. I want it to end in a proper finish.
The stance is a held breath before the first bar. I will know when to let it go: when your weight shifts.
You describe technique like a lullaby. Play the hold for me, and I will hear where it goes wrong.
Strikes are the percussion. Good rhythm, but who keeps time when they stop?
A risk should leave a last note hanging. Otherwise it is only noise between songs.
A stall is a rest with no music in it. A pin needs movement, so I will take it from you.
The crowd came to hear something move. Play them a line they will remember.
You want to be heard. I can hear you, and I can hear where you slip off the beat.
I have listened to your {strength} from the first bar, and I can hear where it stops working.
I have hummed your {strength} twice, and I know the bar where it falters.
You kept your tempo. That is a steady rhythm, and I like it.
Fair. We are humming the same tune from here, and I will take the rest on the mat.
I could raise my voice. I would rather hold the note a little longer.
One fall, one final chord. Keep me down, and the song is yours.
On the mat the tempo gets close. Stay with the beat.
Grounded or standing, the melody still belongs to us.
Stand up where I can hear you. Let the crowd hum along with what you do.
A good answer, in tune. Now let us hear it move.
The room is quiet now. The rest is a silence, and I notice it.
Fair tune, then. That is a moment worth keeping.
I accept that phrase. I will play you the rest at the bell.
I will give this match everything, until the last bar ends.
My approach is precise, and I will play the detail on the night.
Whatever happens, the song will be honest.
The last chord is not written yet. I like that.
I have one more verse, and you will hear it when the bell rings.
